Glogowek Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Głogówek, Poland

Not demolished. Jews are first recorded in Głogówek in 1349, expelled multiple times before a kehilla formed in the second half of the 18th century. Population reached 170 by 1880 before declining to just 50 (0.7%) by 1932. A Progressive-Reform synagogue, built in 1864, joined an earlier synagogue dating to at least 1851; Kristallnacht burned the synagogue and shattered Jewish-owned shop and home windows. In 1942, Głogówek's Jews were transported to the Terezín ghetto. This cemetery's founding date is unknown, though its oldest surviving tombstone (Gitel Löwe, August 19, 1821) confirms its existence by then; the last recorded burial occurred March 15, 1936. Ownership transferred to the Jewish Association of Germany in 1939, then the Gestapo in 1943; postwar neglect and theft further reduced the site.
